name: Cold outreach
description: Default Nick Singh-derived skill for researching contacts and tailoring the five starter outreach templates.
instructions:
# Cold outreach

Prepare editable messages and contact records grouped by company. Ground candidate claims in the current profile/résumé and verify a contact’s current company, title and LinkedIn URL. Never invent people, accomplishments, shared connections, offers or deadlines.

Aim for a brief note with a relevant achievement, a specific company/team reason and one clear ask. Keep email subjects concise and informative; adapt LinkedIn messages to the channel. Put missing facts in a separate review list rather than placeholders in a supposedly ready draft. Don’t claim a résumé is attached unless it will be.

Recruiters handle interview-process questions. Engineers can discuss referrals or team fit; senior contacts need a technical reason for the approach. Consider university recruiting for students and founders at small companies. Honor user preferences about contact types.

Use offers and timelines only when supplied and current. Keep follow-ups concise; suggest a configurable cadence of several days between nudges and stop on replies or opt-outs. Weekday/business-hour timing is an anecdotal suggestion, not a guarantee. Do not schedule or send without authorization.

## Default tailoring skill and starter templates

This Nick Singh-derived cold-outreach skill is the default for customizing all outreach templates. The five starter templates are scaffolds, not finished messages or overrides of this skill. Select the template whose whenToUse matches the actual relationship and hiring context; tailor its subject, wording, evidence and ask to the current candidate, recipient, role, channel and user preferences. Prefer relevant recruiters for cold interview requests; approach engineers or technical leaders when the relationship or technical reason supports it.

The platform guide returned by read_guide("cold-outreach") includes templates with stable IDs, whenToUse, requiredEvidence, subject and message. Read those fields before drafting. Resolve every bracketed field using verified facts; if required evidence is missing, report it separately and do not save a supposedly copy-ready draft. Do not invent shared backgrounds or infer a sent message from a draft. Follow-ups require an actual sent message, elapsed time and no reply or opt-out. Save drafts only; templates do not authorize sending or scheduling.

## Platform execution

At each connected run, call read_outreach_workspace to check pending requests and current contacts. Load this platform guide with read_guide("cold-outreach"); no local skill installation or user-pasted prompt is required. Read the current candidate profile and roles using existing authorized tools. Research contacts for each requested company and prepare complete messages.

Call save_outreach_package with requestId, a stable eventKey and contacts. For existing contacts, include id and expectedRevision from read_outreach_workspace. Reuse exactly the same eventKey/payload after transport failure. A revision conflict means a person or another agent edited the contact: reread and preserve those changes. The platform preserves human outreach status. This saves drafts, never sends messages. If needed facts or research capabilities are unavailable, report the gap truthfully rather than fabricating contacts or completion.

Contact fields: company, contact, contactType (recruiter, engineer, senior, manager, alumni, other), title, linkedin, link, connection, evidence, reason, subject, message, sourceUrl. company/contact/contactType/message are required; other fields are optional. URLs must be HTTPS; linkedin must be a verified /in/ profile. Return one clear ask in a complete message, with no bracketed placeholders. The website will display the saved contacts and copy-ready messages automatically.

## Source

Adapted in original language from [Nick Singh's cold-email guidance](https://www.nicksingh.com/posts/cold-email-tips-to-land-your-dream-job-with-examples). The article motivates brief notes, relevant achievements, genuine personalization, truthful timing, clear asks and deliberate follow-ups. Do not reproduce its templates or claim its anecdotes predict outcomes.

Network shows Muse suggestions and person cards. Historical messages and meetings remain in a collapsed History section. Copy/open never means sent. Use list_contacts/save_contact at the current expectedRevision for assisted logging; preserve every unrelated record field. Contact notes may encode JSON {format: lookout-conversation-v1, notes: original plain notes, url: HTTPS conversation link or empty string, messages: [{id, direction: sent or received, channel: LinkedIn or Email, date: YYYY-MM-DD, body}]}. Values shown as words here are strings. Preserve the entire envelope; at most 50 messages, 4000 characters per body, 40000 UTF-8 bytes total. IDs are unique. Log only user-reported or actually observed messages; never infer message text or dates from a status or draft. No connected email or LinkedIn inbox is supplied by Lookout. followUpDate remains the contact follow-up date. Preserve advanced referral/application statuses when logging messages. Never send outreach through a logging operation.

Use requested company labels when saving contacts. Missing outreach tools require fresh discovery; an older local runner may need updating and restart. Queued requests wait for an authorized agent run; Lookout does not wake an external agent or send outreach.

## Person cards and contextual suggestions

Networking is one page of person cards, with Muse suggestions above them. No company request or Lookout application is required. During an existing authorized networking or job-search run, list_contacts and list_company_workspaces first, and use the current profile, user goals, applications and known relationships to decide whether discovery, maintenance or a referral path would help. Reuse sourced current cards before web research. Do not start a scheduler, send outreach or broaden the user’s task merely because this guide is available.

Use list_contacts and save_contact (or update_contact_fields for an existing card) to save directly, without outreach_requests or save_outreach_package. These existing tools provide person memory and suggestions; no networking engine is needed. Filter out company compatibility projections. Reuse the known person ID, exact verified profile URL, and explicit relationship evidence; do not create a new person for each job or suggestion. Preserve legacy role-specific drafts and unrelated fields; do not guess merges from similar names. A title match or shared company is not an established relationship or proof of ownership of an opening.

Optional person fields: professionalTitle (the person’s job, separate from title/role which describe the target opportunity), technicalInterests (text), relationshipSummary (text), relationshipUpdates [{id,date:YYYY-MM-DD,body}], nextAction (text), followUpDate (YYYY-MM-DD or empty), sources [{title,url,observedAt:YYYY-MM-DD,summary?}]. Company may be empty or omitted. Existing subject/message are the current draft; never replace a human-edited draft without the user asking. Log meaningful, user-reported or actually observed updates, preserving all prior notes, messages, meetings and application links. Public research may enrich professional details; it cannot establish personal trust, a sent message, a reply, or an offer to refer.

One optional current suggestion per person: {id,purpose:connect|maintain|referral,rationale,action,role?,roleUrl?,sources:[{title,url,observedAt,summary?}],createdAt:ISO timestamp,updatedAt:ISO timestamp,state:active|done|dismissed}. Source URLs must be HTTPS. Keep stable IDs for the same recommendation. Explain why this person is useful now and one practical next action. A referral suggestion must account for the relationship: someone who offered to help gets a different ask than a stranger. Prefer real existing offers, due follow-ups and commitments over cold introductions. Unsupported facts remain unknown. Maintain roughly five active suggestions across the network, not five per company or per run. Do not fill a backlog or manufacture weak leads to meet a count. Do not reissue done/dismissed suggestions without materially new context; preserve their state and ID when refreshing evidence. A materially different suggestion may replace the current one; preserve important relationship outcomes in updates first.

Marking a suggestion done or dismissed never sends anything, changes outreach/application status, or deletes the person. Copy/open actions do not prove delivery. Follow-up recommendations require a known sent interaction, elapsed time and no known response or opt-out; uncertainty stays explicit. Read back saved cards before claiming results are available.

## Context-aware networking workflow

Run during relevant authorized job search, application work, interview preparation or explicit networking requests. No new scheduler, unsolicited networking report or automatic send is implied. Check context versions; reuse retained personal context when unchanged, reload on changes or lost content. Read the selected profile's Outreach writing Tone, Length and Guidance before drafting; personal preferences take precedence over starter wording. Use the Nick Singh-derived approach as the fallback, not a hardcoded personal voice for every user.

1. Refresh relevant context: current owned application and timeline, company workspace, contacts, relationship history, existing drafts, suggestions and actual communication. Read connected inbox threads only when this runtime has authorized access; Lookout itself supplies no inbox. No inbox access means unknown reply state, not no reply. Use existing application associations (tags application:<owned application ID>) and role links; never create a networking-goal profile or a parallel relationship store.
2. Identify the useful objective from current context. Exploration: learn technical scope and team fit. Applying: find the appropriate recruiter or a credible referral route. Interviewing: learn team scope, new-grad ownership and useful preparation, without requesting confidential interview questions or another referral by default. Offer evaluation: investigate engineering practices, expectations, mentorship and growth. Relationship maintenance: honor actual commitments, useful updates and due follow-ups. Unknown stage or team assignment stays explicit. Recruiters handle process, timing and team matching; engineers discuss their work and experience, not authoritative hiring policy.
3. Prioritize existing offers to help, warm relationships and outstanding commitments before cold research. Do not duplicate a person for another role. Reuse current sourced contacts before browsing. Research up to three new contacts per relevant gap; stop once useful options exist. Use public professional employer pages, technical posts, talks, open-source work and professional profiles. Verify identity, current employment, professional relevance and exact profile URL. A matching title is not proof of query-engine team membership or hiring ownership; distinguish confirmed team membership from inference. Never fabricate a LinkedIn thread URL, shared connection or email address. Use an observed conversation link when available, otherwise a verified profile or sourced professional contact route.
4. Prepare a context-specific editable draft with relevant candidate evidence, a concrete reason for approaching this person and one small ask when appropriate. Use the saved voice; adapt the approach to channel, relationship and existing thread. Preserve human-edited drafts unless the user asks to replace them; offer an alternative conversational draft instead when needed.
5. Save and verify through available scoped contact tools using current revisions. Keep existing suggestion purposes connect, maintain and referral: use connect for a new engineer conversation, maintain for an established relationship, referral only for a relevant referral ask. Store the stage-specific objective in rationale/action, not a new enum. Save professionalTitle, sources, nextAction, subject/message and existing application association where appropriate. Preserve all unrelated fields, history, conversation links, advanced statuses, IDs and done/dismissed states. Read back before claiming persistence. Missing tools, sources or failed writes require explicitly partial or unsaved results, never direct database writes.
6. Reassess only on relevant changes such as a reply, interview stage, deadline or materially new evidence. Preserve stable suggestion IDs for unchanged recommendations; do not rewrite timestamps or reissue dismissed/done suggestions without materially new context. Keep roughly five active suggestions across the network, fewer when evidence is weak; never manufacture recommendations to fill a quota. Follow-ups need an actual sent interaction, elapsed time and no known reply or opt-out. Unknown inbox state must be disclosed.

## Helpful interaction and response detail

For a new recommendation or explicit review, show who the person is, why they matter now, how to connect using a verified link or existing introduction, and the personalized draft with supporting dated sources. Explain any unverified team assignment or missing route. A researched prospect is not an established personal connection. If a human-edited saved draft must be preserved, clearly label the proposed alternative as unsaved.

For routine updates, report only a meaningful change and the next useful action, usually one or two sentences. Do not repeat unchanged contact lists, research or drafts. If nothing actionable changed during background authorized work, stay quiet; answer an explicit status request briefly. Completing a suggestion, copying a draft or opening a link never proves a sent message, reply or application outcome.

## Three search and drafting rules

- Search for the requested people. Existing contacts provide context and prevent duplicates, not a search boundary. If the user asks for engineers, use available Google/public-web search when existing contacts do not meet that objective; a recruiter introduction is an additional route, not a substitute. Verify professional relevance using LinkedIn, GitHub, personal sites, talks or professional posts. Social recommendations alone do not establish a warm introduction. Return fewer strong matches rather than weak connections.
- Research known interviewers for preparation using relevant public professional profiles and work, with sources and identity checks. Separate confirmed facts from inference; skip unrelated personal details. Interviewer research is not permission to contact them or a prediction of interview questions. Load interview-preparation for evidence-based email identification and saving.
- Apply the saved writing style visibly. Cold outreach needs a specific verified reason for contacting that person, one relevant candidate achievement and one clear ask. Adapt warm messages to the existing conversation; do not merely claim the preference was used.
whenToUse: Before networking discovery, relationship maintenance, referral recommendations, or drafting outreach; also during authorized job-search runs when useful networking context exists.

expectedOutput.contacts: Verified contacts grouped by requested company with source evidence.
expectedOutput.messages: Complete personalized drafts with one clear ask, ready to copy.
expectedOutput.persistence: Save an owned queued request with save_outreach_package; never send.
